title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Having secured absolute dominion over the world, Gwyn thus began the Age of Fire, a time of prosperity that was characterized by the power of the First Flame and the vision of the Great Lord. Gwyn's clan placed themselves atop the new world order, assuming the role of deities for humans who were their subjects, and Gwyn took the title "god of sunlight". Humans venerated the gods who lived in the city of Anor Londo in the region of Lordran, building an economy and culture around the use of souls, even hunting the descendants of dragons for sport and domesticating some of them. Gwyn left the other two Lords to tend to their own domains: Izalith built her civilization underground where she and her daughters continued to study flame sorcery, and Gravelord Nito remained in the Catacombs to oversee the dead.

title: Lore
snippet:
Lore -  Dark Souls - storyline - the_age_of_fire 
 the_age_of_fire : After the defeat of the Everlasting Dragons Gwyn established the land of Lordran and granted Seath the title of "Duke" along with a part of his Lord Soul for his contribution in the war. He also gave another part of his Lord Soul as well as the titles of "King" to the Four Kings, the leaders of New Londo, in recognition of their foresight. Gwyn resided in the capital city of Anor Londo and had three children:
Lord Gwyn's Firstborn, Old God of War, who was stripped of his deific status and erased from history for his foolishness. He is closely related to the Warrior of Sunlight covenant and inherited the sunlight from his father. In an age long after this one, their identity was revealed to be the Nameless King.
Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight, who later married Flame God Flann (and presumably left the land with him).
Dark Sun Gwyndolin, who was raised as a girl for his affection to the moon.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Although the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods lasted for centuries, at some point the First Flame began to fade. Gwyn understood that if the Flame went out, the Age of Fire would be succeeded by an Age of Dark, a new order of humans led by a Dark Lord. Fearful of this outcome, the god made a drastic decision: In order to maintain the order of Gods, he would sacrifice himself to link the dying Flame and prolong its life. He trusted none but himself to carry out the sacrifice involved; he thus divided the power of his Lord Soul among the members of his clan and handed down the power of the sun to his children, leaving his firstborn son to inherit his titles. Gwyn also tasked his sons and Frampt with shepherding the humans into following his example, linking the Flame generation after generation, to uphold his Age of Fire, each of them becoming Lords through the process.

title: Lore
snippet:
Gwyn, in a final effort to save the Age of Fire, marches with a great deal of his army to the Kiln of the First Flame and sacrifices himself to link with the First Flame, turning the Kiln to ash and incinerating his entire army (making them the Black Knights, who later walk Lordran). The attempt is temporarily successful, however, as the Age of Fire was only extended for at least 1000 years. Gwyn became a Hollow and is from then on known as "Gwyn, Lord of Cinder".

The Four Kings became corrupted and were seduced by evil at some point by Kaathe after Gwyn's fall and their servants turned into Darkwraiths. In an effort to stop them New Londo was flooded with all of its population, trapping the Four Kings with their Darkwraiths in the Abyss.

Soon after, the deities began leaving Lordran. Gwyndolin was the only one of Gwyn's children to stay behind...

title: Lord Gwyn's Firstborn
snippet:
Lord Gwyn's Firstborn -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Lord Gwyn's firstborn, the God of War, inherited the sunlight from his father, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight. He once wore an ancient ring capable of boosting the strength of miracles. He was said to have had respect only for arms and nothing else, and wielded the Sunlight Blade and Great Lightning Spear miracles.

His foolishness led to the stripping of his deific status and the expunging of his existence from history, with his name being forgotten. Sunlight Blade, which had the power to boost a weapon with rays of the sun in the form of lightning, was left on Gwyn's coffin, perhaps as a final farewell.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin at some point learned of Gwyn's existence and his story but not his name, referring to him merely as the "Lord of Light". He understood how Gwyn altered the natural order and began linking the Flame, which extended the Age of Fire against the course of nature, and he expresses his outrage at Gwyn for making men lesser than their original form as the "Lord of Light" banished Dark and all that stemmed from Humanity with the Darksign, defining it as the "First Sin" committed against humans and their nature.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet:
Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Gwynevere is the first daughter of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and one of the deities who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire. She was worshipped by the humans as the "goddess of sunlight" and a symbol of bounty and fertility, while she was also cherished by all the other gods. As a goddess of sunlight, her miracles of Bountiful Sunlight and Soothing Sunlight were able to convey the sun's rays to heal, a blessing she granted to many warriors. She also taught her miracles to her maidens and created holy water with healing properties thanks to her light. Gwynevere was venerated in a church alongside the main cathedral of Anor Londo; the structure was also used to contain the Painted World of Ariamis, protected by the Painting Guardians.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Ages past his linking of the First Flame, Gwyn's very name was lost. Even his miracles recounting his battles with lightning spears against the dragons at the start of the Age of Fire do not mention his name, implying that his heritage and culture have been lost to Drangleic. In fact, the only knowledge of a "god of the sun" leading the clan of the gods comes from the miracles that narrate the deeds of his son, who became king and god of the sun after him but was then exiled and deprived of his name.

However in Heide, as the beacon of the culture of Anor Londo in the region, there are several statues representing him, albeit in a distorted form but resembling the characteristics of Gwyn's representations in Lordran. Although portrayed with the head of an eagle, the pose, the sun medallion and the sword still strongly resemble the weapon, robes and symbology of the Lord of Sunlight.

title: Soul of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Soul of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and Cinder, who linked the First Flame.

Lord Gwyn bequeathed most of his power to the Gods, and burned as cinder for the First Flame, but even so, Lord Gwyn's soul is a powerful thing indeed.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Gwyn proved himself a skilled ruler, using his power to bind and hold close to him the potential powers of the world. He amply rewarded the betrayal of the dragon Seath and his indispensable contribution to the war, giving him the title of Duke and inducting him into the nobility of the gods through a marriage to one of his daughters. Gwyn also gave him a fragment of his powerful Lord Soul along with the Archives, and left him to his studies near Anor Londo. As for humans, cognizant of the abilities of four of their great leaders, Gwyn bequeathed on them another shard of his powerful Soul, and let them build their civilization of New Londo near the divine capital. Gwyn would also befriend the Primordial Serpent Frampt and convince him of his ideals and vision of the Age of Fire..

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Gwyndolin is the lastborn child of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and one of the deities who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire, although his legitimacy as such only came from being a child of his father. He was worshipped as the "God of the Darkmoon" and held the title of "God of the Dark Sun".

Despite being the son of Gwyn, Gwyndolin was born with a strong moon power, and "weak and repulsive" in appearance, particularly due to the snakes coiled around his lower half. Because of his darkmoon powers and his strong affinity for moon magic, as well as his lineage, Gwyndolin was raised as a female. While still young, Gwyn made him wear women's clothing and gave him a magic ring which would allow Gwyndolin to move and act in a feminine way, leading him to behave "like a dark and fleeting goddess".

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Gwyn is one of the primordial humanoid creatures that appeared underground after the First Flame appeared, bringing life, death and disparity. He was among those who found the four Lord Souls, sources of immense power, together with Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith and the Furtive Pygmy.

With the immense power of his soul, the greatest among all the Lords, Gwyn established an underground civilization, becoming its ruler and forming an army of Silver Knights. At some point Gwyn had a relationship with an unknown woman and from their union were born his firstborn son and his eldest daughter, Gwynevere.

title: Lord Gwyn's Firstborn
snippet:
Lord Gwyn's Firstborn -  Dark Souls - character - warriors_of_sunlight 
 warriors_of_sunlight : Gwyn's firstborn shares his symbol with the Warrior of Sunlight covenant, the Sunlight Medal. The covenant itself is closely related to the firstborn, the members being referred to as his warriors, and the god is said to watch over the covenant closely. Assuming the player meets the correct requisites, it is possible to join by praying at the Sunlight Altar, located in the Undead Parish, or by talking to Solaire of Astora, a fanatical member.

The covenant and symbol both survived into the times of Drangleic and Lothric. In Lothric, the symbol on the sunlight medals was considered holy.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: After his father Gwyn linked the First Flame, his throne passed to his firstborn son who, treacherously, chose to "ally" with the ancient dragons, the ancient enemies of the gods, and was therefore dethroned, exiled and his name eradicated from history. Following these events, his sister Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight abandoned Anor Londo together with nearly all of the other deities, leaving Gwyndolin as the last remaining deity in the city. Despite being the last son of the royal family of the gods, Gwyndolin was psychologically unfit to become the next ruler, still playing the feminine role imposed on him by his father Gwyn, leaving Lloyd to take advantage of the situation who proclaimed himself king of the gods, justified by his being Gwyn's uncle, and become the chief deity of the Way of White.

title: Lore
snippet:
Lore -  Dark Souls - storyline - the_first_flame 
 the_first_flame : The advent of fire occurred, and with it came heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. The First Flame was born, source of all fire. However, from the dark came humanoid creatures - Hollows. These creatures found the Lord Souls near the flames and took on the powers they gave. They were:
Gravelord Nito, The First of the Dead, who offered much of his own soul to death, granting him the ability to administer the death of all life.
The Witch of Izalith, who became the leader of the flame sorcerers, later the so-called "Daughters of Chaos".
Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, who was to achieve great things in his life.
A fourth unique Lord Soul called the "Dark Soul" was found by the Furtive Pygmy, who is the ancestor of the humans. They are supposed to bring about the Age of Dark, in which humanity rules the world. A distant descendant of him is the Chosen Undead.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Gwyn's act of linking the First Flame came to be a point of controversy for several figures; namely Kaathe and Aldia would regard Gwyn's sacrifice as having "unnaturally" extended an Age of Fire that was never meant to last, inhibiting the potential of humans in the process. As of the time of the Chosen Undead, one consequence of Kaathe's actions lies beneath Firelink Shrine: the ruins of New Londo, which was captured by the Darkstalker and had to be flooded before the Abyss within could spread to the surface world.

title: Gods
snippet:
Lord Gwyn, God of Sunlight, who claimed a Lord Soul, conquered the world after defeating the Dragons and ruled it as king of the Gods. He eventually sacrificed himself to Link the First Flame, becoming the first Lord of Cinder, with his empty husk guarding the Flame. He is regarded as the omnipotent main deity of the Way of White, the faith worshipping the Gods of Anor Londo.
Gwyn's Firstborn Son, once a God of War and of the Sun, who had originally inherited Gwyn's throne and ruled Anor Londo. However, he would later be cast out and stripped of his status as a deity, his faith becoming anathema to the Way of White while he became a nameless king, with all traces of him erased from history. He was succeeded by Lloyd as ruler of the Gods. His symbol is that of a sun.

title: Furtive Pygmy
snippet: As Gwyn's war against the Dragons proved costly for his forces, the Lord of Sunlight was forced to integrate into his ranks the Ringed Knights, descendants of the Furtive Pygmy who had developed their own weapons and armor vitalized by the Abyss. With their combined might, the four Lords eventually defeated the dragons, beginning a new age.

title: Lords
snippet:
Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - gwyn_lord_of_cinder 
 gwyn_lord_of_cinder : Gwyn used the power granted from the Lord Soul to create bolts of sunlight that he used to peel the scales from the dragons. His race has wildly varied physical appearances, though most have whitish skin and are usually taller than humans, however there are many exceptions to this standard.

Gwyn became the king of Lordran, and he bestowed fragments of his Lord Soul to Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Seath, and the Four Kings of New Londo. He had four loyal knights and a host of Silver Knights. His executioner, Smough, also wished to become a knight but was seen as unfit due to his cannibalism.

In his fear of the Age of Dark, he sacrificed himself to the First Flame, prolonging the Age of Fire and becoming Lord of Cinder. This act rendered Gwyn Hollow.

title: Furtive Pygmy
snippet: While the Lords emerged victorious and were free to carve out their new domains, Great Lord Gwyn was evidently afraid of the Dark Soul. His dominion was threatened by the life-generating capabilities of the Abyss—it was similar to the First Flame, with a key exception: it had seemingly endless potential, as it lost little to no power when divided unlike Gwyn's own Lord Soul. The Lord of Sunlight resolved the issue through skillful diplomacy: He gifted the Pygmies a city at the edge of the world, along with his daughter Filianore as a token of their pact. Gwyn's generosity was cause for much gratitude among the Pygmies, which manifested as veneration and prostration to the Great Lord. His daughter Filianore became an object of worship within the Ringed City, for whom a church was established wherein she could slumber peacefully, "all for the sake of man". title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Now bereft of most of his Lord Soul's power and with only the power of his soul, Gwyn left for the Kiln of the First Flame, the structure built to house and protect it, with only his robes, his mighty greatsword and his powerless crown, accompanied only by a guard of Black Knights. Eventually Gwyn linked the First Flame, prolonging its life but himself being consumed by it, reduced to the empty husk of cinders guarding the core of the Kiln. The inferno of the newly kindled fire melted the surroundings and burned his knights to ashes, leaving them to wander the world as disembodied spirits.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: At some point, Gwyn would create a powerful miracle able to create an immense mass of souls and transform it into an orb of light, resembling the sun, that could release lightning. The miracle was developed from Gwyn's emotion of either hatred or sorrow but curiously, it would be forbidden by the same God that created it.

title: Lords
snippet:
Fearing the upcoming Age of Dark and potentially humans as well, Gwyn took some of his knights with him left to the Kiln of the First Flame, sacrificing himself to rekindle the First Flame. The Black Knights who followed after Gwyn were reduced to ash, and Gwyn himself became hollow.

The extension of the Age of Fire was not without consequences. As a result, the undead curse arose from Gwyn's actions. Humans who were afflicted by the curse bore the Darksign. Those that bore it would be revived after death, though their humanity would be lost, and without restoring it would eventually lose their sanity.

title: Lords
snippet:
Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - age_of_disparity 
 age_of_disparity : Little is known of the lives of the Lords before the discovery of Fire. Gwyn had an uncle in Allfather Lloyd, and The Witch was accompanied by her adult daughters when she claimed her soul, so it is possible they may have existed before claiming their Lord Souls.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Gwyn's title uses the kanji "薪の王" that can be literally translated as "King of Kindling" or "King of Firewood".
Gwyn's design and lore seems to have been heavily inspired by Zeus of ancient Greek mythology.
Several aspects of him can also be compared to the Welsh deity Gwyn ap Nudd.
**Gwyn ap Nudd is said to be a warrior with a "blackened face" similar to Gwyn's hollowed flesh, and the King of the "fair folk." The gods of Lordran being a fair folk.
**In Arthurian legends and writings, Gwyn ap Nudd was the ruler of a delightful paradise called the otherworld, or Annwn. Such a place would be similar to Anor Londo during its glory days.
**Additionally, one can make a comparison between Gwyn ap Nudd leading the Wild Hunt in Welsh legend, and the dragon hunts of Gwyn.
"Gwyn" translated from Welsh means "White/Pure" or "Holy".

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : Lord Gwyn wears an impressive set of royal drapes, with gold bands on his arms, and a crown atop his head. On his feet are what appear to be a form of moccasins and anklets, and he wields a greatsword imbued with the power of light and of the First Flame, which he uses to adequate effect. His face is that of an aged man with calm eyes, and he has an impressively long, grey beard and hair of the same nature. When the Chosen Undead fights Gwyn in the Kiln of the First Flame, Gwyn is nothing more than an empty husk with a haggard appearance, charred skin and hollowed eyes.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: Gwyndolin created an illusory image of his sister Gwynevere, to govern through her cherished figure and covering for her departure, taking upon himself to lead what remained of his father's kingdom and the Silver Knights through this illusion, though he didn't attempt to claim the throne for himself. Gwyndolin also collaborated with Kingseeker Frampt to maintain the system and religion created by his father to keep the First Flame and the Age of Fire alive. Together they used the illusion of Gwynevere to seek a worthy champion to link the Flame again, creating a prophecy which they hoped to make self-fulfilling by guiding and manipulating those who passed their various challenges and earned the Lordvessel, a component required to access the Kiln of the First Flame, while also maintaining some semblance of divinity and control over the ancient city.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Age of Fire -  Dark Souls - storyline - description 
 description : **WARNING: This entire page lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations to be considered even useful**

The Age of Fire first began after Gwyn and the other Lords defeated the Everlasting Dragons which ended the Age of Ancients. The Age of Fire was unnaturally prolonged when Gwyn sacrificed himself to kindle the First Flame.

When the Chosen Undead talks to Kingseeker Frampt, he will tell them that they are destined to succeed Gwyn. Should the player choose to kindle the First Flame upon the defeat of Gwyn, they will sacrifice themselves as Gwyn did, thus delaying the Age of Dark once more.

Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

Taking advantage of the situation, Lloyd, as Gwyn's uncle, took power, proclaiming himself king of the gods.He then became the main deity of the religion, known as the god of Law and Caste and his face was even minted on the golden coins used by men.

snippet:

title: The Nameless King
snippet: The eldest son of Gwyn eventually decided to "sacrifice everything" to ally himself with the dragons. In the eyes of the other deities of Anor Londo, archenemies of the dragons, his actions amounted to an unforgivable sin; he was therefore dethroned and exiled from the city. The former king was deprived of his deific status, his statues destroyed and his name erased from the annals of history. Before leaving Anor Londo, the eldest left his sunlight blade miracle and ring on Gwyn's empty tomb in his mausoleum as a final farewell, still paying respects for his father. Now excommunicated from the pantheon of the gods and without a home, the god of war continued to watch closely over his warriors of the sunlight, listening to their prayers and rewarding the proofs of their exploits with his miracles of Sunlight Spear and Great Lightning Spear.

title: Lore
snippet:
Soon after, the deities began leaving Lordran. Gwyndolin was the only one of Gwyn's children to stay behind...

Seath, who became obsessed with his research and experiments, amassed countless tomes and was eventually driven mad - at least, how normal people see it - by his research, becoming the founder of sorcery.

At least a thousand years pass and the events of "Dark Souls" begin to unfold...

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: It may be hard for the player to find a proper opening to fight back or heal as a result of Gwyn actively seeking the player. Despite his very weakened state, he is still the former Lord of Sunlight, so don't rely on lightning as he is immune. His attacks deal a great amount of damage if they connect. If blocked, his attacks will still deal considerable damage to the player as a result of the flame damage his sword deals. A good way to reduce the damage to a slight margin is by using shields with high fire defense, such as the Black Iron Greatshield or the Black Knight Shield, which can be dropped by the nearby Black Knights; however, care should still be taken as blocking a full attack chain will cost a lot of stamina and may eventually result in losing health or dying. The Gold-Hemmed Black Set can further negate the fire damage at the cost of less physical defense against his attacks.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : The remnants of the will and power of Gwyn, as the first one to ever link the First Flame, would emerge as part of the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who have linked themselves to the First Flame throughout history, thus creating a hollowed-out entity possessing all the abilities of the previous Champions.

The powers of Gwyn would manifest when the Soul of Cinder was challenged by an aspiring Champion; acting as the Flame's last line of defense within the Kiln, the Soul of Cinder fought to either test the might of one who would link the Flame, or to protect it from a would-be betrayer or usurper.

title: Timeline
snippet:
Gwyn takes the more powerful Lord Soul and becomes the Lord of Sunlight.
Thanks to the power of their immense souls, the Lords expand their power and develops their civilizations underground.
The nameless blacksmith deity begins using titanite to forge the weapons and armor of the Lords.
Gwyn creates his army of Silver Knights.
The Nameless King is the first son of Lord Gwyn.
Gwynevere is the first daughter of Lord Gwyn.
The Witch of Izalith gives birth to a number of children and shares her fire sorcery with them.
Nito becomes capable of producing deadly miasmas.
Seath is born, a unique dragon different from the others, scaleless, pale and mortal because of the disparity.
A Pygmy takes the last Lord Soul, the Dark Soul, much later than the other Lords.
The Pygmy splits the Dark Soul, sharing it with his kin and creating the Humans, a naturally immortal race thanks to the fragments of the Dark Soul inside each of them.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet:

Gwyn skillfully resolved the issue through diplomacy: He gifted the pygmies a magnificent ringed city at the edge of the world, as well as his youngest daughter Filianore as part of their pact. With this clever move Gwyn ensured that the Pygmy Lords and the power of their Dark Soul would be contained within the Ringed City and out of history, whilst making them subjects to his dominion, eliminating from the annals even the contributions of the Ringed Knights during the war against the dragons and the very existence of the Furtive Pygmy. Gwyn thus used his Great Soul to manipulate the light of the sun, transforming rays of sunlight into lightning, a form of energy capable of penetrating dragon scales. Meeting the dragons in battle, Gwyn used his spears of sunlight to peel apart the dragons' scales, while his knights employed lightning-infused weapons to similar effect. The Witch of Izalith and her daughters weaved great firestorms, destroying the archtrees and burning the dragons; while Nito unleashed a miasma of death, rotting the archtrees and infecting the dragons. title: Giants (Lore)
snippet: After the end of the great war, Lord Gwyn and his clan gained dominion over the world and began their Age of Fire, with the giants continuing to coexist with their civilization in a subordinate but close position. A number of giants became Sentinels guarding the walls and streets of Anor Londo, the city of the gods, employing giant halberds made of brass and retaining the power of lightning, giant shields of white iron, and heavy armor of finely decorated golden brass. An even more powerful group of giants defended the royal cathedral in the center of the city and were capable of performing restorative and offensive miracles.

Before the Age of Fire was the Age of Ancients. It was a time in which the world was colorless and shrouded by fog. The land consisted of gray crags, archtrees and Everlasting Dragons, who were the rulers of the world. Humans and other creatures had yet to make an impression upon the world.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Once his army had been prepared and armed with spears and greatbows that used arrows as big as iron spears, Gwyn went to the surface with the intention of waging war against the Dragons and conquering the world with his Lord allies. The war turned out to be very bloody; for each of the majestic creatures slain, three scores of Gwyn's soldiers perished. The bodies of dragons were harder than stone, and resistant to fire and magic, making their killing difficult. At one point Gwyn was even forced to integrate into his ranks the primordial humans, descendants of the Furtive Pygmy who had found the Dark Soul, and who had developed their own weapons and armor infused with the life-giving power of the Abyss.

title: Lord Gwyn's Firstborn
snippet:
Long ago, the Nameless King was a god of war and heir to lightning. The firstborn was a god of war, and inherited sunlight, which manifests as lightning.
The Nameless King wielded the Dragonslayer Swordspear, a weapon from the Age of Gods. The firstborn similarly wielded a great spear.
The firstborn eventually committed a grave error in the eyes of Anor Londo, which led to the rescinding of his deific status and his removal from the annals of history, his name forgotten. The Nameless King sacrificed everything to ally with the ancient dragons, whom he once fought.
The Nameless King wore a crown and bracelets that greatly resemble those once worn by Gwyn, the First Lord.
Dragon Slayer Ornstein, once the faithful first knight of the Sun's firstborn, left Anor Londo in the dragonless age in search of the Nameless King. His weapon, a cross spear, is extremely similar to that wielded by the Nameless King.

title: Gods
snippet: Gwyn derived the bulk of his power and influence from the First Flame, which he shared with the other gods, but in time the Flame began to die. To preserve their influence over the world, Gwyn sacrificed himself by entering the Kiln of the First Flame, where his strength would keep the Flame alive.

title: First Flame
snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. Gwyn's clan linked the sacred bonfires that were tied to the Flame to humanity, and shepherded the humans who worshipped them to kindle the flames. The Witch of Izalith attempted to use her own powerful soul to create a new First Flame, but this attempt failed, instead creating the perverse Flame of Chaos and transforming the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, which would go on to birth the race of Demons.

title: First Flame
snippet:
Aware that time was quickly running out for his kingdom, Gwyn and a detachment of his knights entered the Kiln of the First Flame. The knights stood guard as Gwyn sacrificed himself to the waning Flame at the Kiln's centre. This immediately reinvigorated the First Flame, creating a firestorm that turned the Kiln to ash, and incinerated all of Gwyn's knights, creating the Black Knights and dooming them to wander the lands as disembodied spirits forever after.

Gwyn's sacrifice succeeded in perpetuating the Age of Fire for a time, but *Dark Souls* takes place at least 1000 years later, and the Flame is quickly fading once again. Soon, only Dark will remain.

title: Allfather Lloyd
snippet: Before the Lord of Sunlight sacrificed himself to link the First Flame, he divided his power among his family, instructed his sons to lead humanity and passed down his sunlight and title to his firstborn. However, his son would eventually be exiled and erased from history due to his actions, and taking advantage of the situation, Lloyd would proclaim himself "Allfather", leader of all the other gods and main figure of the Way of White. His claim remained unopposed, despite his grandnephew Gwyndolin having a stronger case for inheriting the position seeing as it was the religion of Gwyn's immediate family. Sadly, the reclusive god still viewed himself as repulsive and unworthy of his father's legacy and the task he had bestowed upon him.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gwynevere, Goddess of Sunlight and eldest daughter of Gwyn. She fled Anor Londo prior to the events of *Dark Souls*, after which she married the God Flann, with whom she had several children. By the time of *Dark Souls III*, she married King Oceiros, making her the Queen of Anor Londo's neighbouring kingdom of Lothric, and mothered three of his children, although she has fled this kingdom too by the events of the game.
Gwyndolin, God of the "Dark Moon" and of the "Dark Sun", and lastborn son of Gwyn. Raised in secrecy as a girl, he is a hybrid likely mothered by Crossbreed Priscilla, and the last God left in Anor Londo and Lordran by the events of *Dark Souls*, although he remains perceived as somewhat of a minor deity, acting from the shadows, including by creating an illusion of Gwynevere. By the events of *Dark Souls III*, he succeeded Lloyd as ruler of the Gods, and reigned from Irithyll, their new seat of power he built atop old Anor Londo.

title: Velka, Goddess of Sin
snippet: At some point after Gwyn linked the First Flame and Gwyn's firstborn son was dethroned and exiled, she abandoned Anor Londo along with nearly all of the other deities and moved to an unknown location. She continued to collaborate with Dark Sun Gwyndolin and his Blades of the Darkmoon, knights tasked with hunting down blasphemers to inspire fear and respect for the gods. The Goddess of Sin determined the sinners and marked them on her Book of the Guilty so that one day they would face the wrath of the Blades of the Darkmoon; Gwyndolin's followers would cut off an ear from the corpse of the sinners they vanquished, bringing them to their god as proof of their task accomplished.

title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet: The old knights of Lothric also turned to the Firstborn of Lord Gwyn for aid, once venerated as a god of war and the sun, who in turn gave them the tools to face the wyverns. From the sun god they would learn how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons developed in the war between the gods and the Everlasting Dragons. They also learned of his miracles on manipulating lightning as a weapon.

title: Lothric
snippet: The new inhabitants of the region soon found themselves facing large numbers of wyverns and had to rise to the challenge, ascending common knighthood. The old knights of Lothric turned to the Firstborn of Lord Gwyn for aid, once venerated as a god of war and the sun, and built an altar for him in their city, beginning to worship the ancient deity who in return gave them the tools to face the wyverns. From the sun god they would learn how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons developed in the war between the gods and the Everlasting Dragons. They also learned of his miracles on manipulating lightning as a weapon.

title: Dragon Slayer Ornstein
snippet: At some point after Gwyn linked the First Flame and Gwyn's firstborn son was dethroned and exiled, nearly all of the deities abandoned Anor Londo and moved to an unknown location. Ornstein seemingly remained in the forsaken city alongside Executioner Smough to guard the cathedral where Gwynevere, the Princess of Sunlight resided.

title: First Flame
snippet: But then, somewhere in the hollows deep underground, a great and primordial fire that would come to be known as the First Flame burst into being. In doing so, it brought disparities into the world for the first time, such as heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. Soon, humanoid creatures emerged from the darkness surrounding the First Flame, attracted by the fire. These creatures found sources of power called souls near the Flame, and took on the diverse powers the souls gave them. With the strength of four particularly powerful souls, four figures were born: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight, and the Furtive Pygmy. Using their newfound power, these Lords and their forces overthrew the ancient dragons, ushering in the Age of Fire.

title: Timeline
snippet:
Gwyndolin, all too aware of his fragile and repulsive appearance, prefers to create an illusion of his sister Gwynevere, to govern through her cherished figure and covering for her escape.
Gwyndolin is worshiped as the deity of the Dark Sun and becomes the head of Blade of the Darkmoon Covenant, a group of warriors tasked with taking his vengeance on humans branded as sinners by the Goddess Velka and protecting the capital Anor Londo
Gwyndolin continue to carry out his duties remaining segregated in his father's mausoleum without showing himself or claiming Gwyn's throne for himself

title: Gods
snippet:
Filianore, lastborn daughter of Gwyn. It is unclear if she was ever deified, or even if her existence was known to the rest of the world, but her endless slumber in the Ringed City is considered holy by those within and protected by Gwyn's Spears of the Church.
Lloyd, God of Law and Caste, and Gwyn's uncle. By the events of *Dark Souls*, Lloyd is the leader of the Way of White, having proclaimed himself "Allfather Lloyd" after Gwyn's Firstborn was undeified and cast out. By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Gwyndolin took the status of leader of the Gods from him, reforming the Way of White to turn Lloyd's worship anathema.
Velka, Goddess of Sin, tasked with defining sins and overseeing punishment or pardon for them. She is often associated with crows.
Flann, God of Flame. After most of the gods left Anor Londo, he married Gwynevere and had several children with her.
McLoyf, God of Medicine and Alcoholic Drinks. He is nicknamed 'Old Man' McLloyf, although it is not his official title.

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet: Considering that those who had deceived Gundyr had given him his halberd and charged him with linking the Flame, they must have had a position superior to the king of Lothric but still close to him. This could point to the involvement of Gwyndolin, king of the gods of Irithyll, who had strong ties to Lothric; or the Primordial Serpents, who were already advisors to the royal family. Using Gundyr as a golem to test the strength of future Champions would ensure that those overseeing the linking of the Flame would be guaranteed to find potential Lords with enough power to prolong the Age of Fire.

title: Humans
snippet: Over time, others would repeat Gwyn's sacrifice—either for their own reasons or to follow in his footsteps—to rekindle the First Flame. As the First Flame was not intended to burn as long as it had, the fabric of reality began to suffer.

 trivia : Gwyn's parents are never mentioned, despite Lloyd being referred to as his uncle.
The actual order of birth of Gwyn's children is unclear, besides Gwyndolin being younger than both Gwyn's Firstborn Son and Gwynevere, and Fillianore being younger than Gwynevere; Gwyndolin is sometimes referenced as the last child of Gwyn in the first game, but as it is possible that Filianore's very existence is unknown to most, this might be a reflection of erroneous belief, and Filianore might be younger. Although Gwyn's Firstborn Son inherited the rule of the Gods from him, he might have been younger than Gwynevere yet inherited the throne from the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primogeniture#Male-preference_(cognatic)_primogeniture male-preference primogeniture] system used in many real-life monarchies.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gods -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : After Lord Gwyn entered the Kiln of the First Flame, most of the gods abandoned Anor Londo, leaving behind a small army of Silver Knights and two elite knights: Dragon Slayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough, to protect the city. Much more shady was the role of Gwyndolin, the only true God that remained in Anor Londo. He created an illusion of Gwynevere, Lord Gwyn's daughter, to hide the fact that she had left Anor Londo and married the Flame God, Flann. Gwyndolin has the same goal as Kingseeker Frampt, using the illusion of Gwynevere to convince the Chosen Undead to rekindle the First Flame. Gwyndolin seems to survive the events of *Dark Souls* as he is being consumed by Aldrich, Devourer of Gods in *Dark Souls III*, implying that the Chosen Undead either did not fight him or only defeated an illusion of him in the timeline canon to the latter game.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gods -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Even after the awakening of the Ashen One, the influence of several gods or their descendants is still present in the world.

Dark Sun Gwyndolin, once the king of the gods and of Irithyll, had been imprisoned in the city's old cathedral by Pontiff Sulyvahn, that stripped him of his power to rule in his place. However Aldrich, Devourer of Gods had arrived in Irithyll and, after defeating Sulyvahn, he began to devour Gwyndolin. Yorshka, Gwyndolin'sister, is still alive and leads the knights's of the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant, but she has been imprisoned by Sulyvahn in an isolated tower.

title: Timeline
snippet:
Centuries after Lord Gwyn's sacrifice, the First Flame begins to fade again
Lord Gwyn's firstborn, as Gwyn's eldest son, ascends the throne of Anor Londo
Lord Gwyn's firstborn, betrays his bloodline and allies himself with the Dragons, and is eventually deemed unworthy to succeed his father's throne and is exiled
All traces of his existence are purged from the culture and architecture of Gwyn's kingdom, yet he continues to watch over his warriors
Princess Gwynevere abandons Anor Londo along with many other of the deities who resided there
Gwyndolin, as the last remaining member of the royal family, takes it upon himself to lead what remains of his father's kingdom.
Gwyndolin, all too aware of his fragile and repulsive appearance, prefers to create an illusion of his sister Gwynevere, to govern through her cherished figure and covering for her escape.

title: Gods
snippet:
It is unknown if the size of the illusion of Gwynevere in *Dark Souls* is accurate, as she does not appear in person in any of the games lore-wise, and only as an illusion, statue or painting.
Flame God Flann might have not been a God of Anor Londo; he is only mentioned in the description of the Ring of the Sun Princess in *Dark Souls*, which states that after leaving Anor Londo, Gwynevere "became wife to Flame God Flann". No item directly associated with Flann is ever found in the games, and he might have never actually been in Anor Londo, and instead a foreign deity, possibly deified only upon marrying Gwynevere. What became of Gwynevere's marriage to Flann is unknown, but although the Sun Princess Ring's description mentions that after leaving Gwynevere also became "a mother, raising several heavenly children".

title: Dark Soul
snippet: Near the end of the Age of Fire, a slave knight called Gael traveled to the Ringed City, seeking the Pygmy Lords to gain their blood. The blood of the Dark Soul was intended to be used to paint a new Painted World, but to Gael's shock, Filianore's spell was broken and the Pygmy Lords were aged to the point that their blood did not flow, for it was dried in their veins. Even though he knew he had not the strength to survive bearing it, Gael slew the Pygmy Lords and drank from their wounds, absorbing the Dark Soul into himself. It imbued him with a dark miasma and warped his mind, but in the end he was successful, slain by the Ashen One to extract the soul's blood. The current state of the Dark Soul is unknown, but given the eternal nature of Lord Souls, it is unlikely that it was truly destroyed.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: Sometime after Lord Gwyn sacrificed himself to link the fading First Flame, the Primordial Serpent Kaathe began searching for a human strong enough to become the Dark Lord capable of leading humans and usher in an Age of Dark. Kaathe eventually arrived in New Londo and managed to entice the Four Kings, powerful humans who had received a fragment of Gwyn's Lord Soul, into following his ideals, teaching them the art of Lifedrain. The Serpent's dark influence extended to their entire army: The knights of New Londo became Darkwraiths, servants of the Dark who learned the art of Lifedrain and used it to absorb humanity. The Four Kings opened an Abyss in the center of their city, with their Darkwraiths beginning to employ the Red Eye Orbs granted by Kaathe to plunder humanity and expand the reach of the Abyss.

title: Lords
snippet:
Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - dragon_war 
 dragon_war : With the strength given to them by the Lord Souls, the three waged a war on the Everlasting Dragons. They were joined by Seath, a scaleless albino dragon that pillaged the Primordial Crystal from them as well and turned on his own kind.

To combat the dragons, Gwyn released grand bolts of light so powerful that they stripped the dragons of their stone scales. With her daughters, the Witch wove firestorms that incinerated the land. Once this was done, Nito arrived for the killing blow by releasing the miasma of death upon the dragons. Soon the dragons were defeated - but not gone - and the Age of Fire began.
Even after the war, Gwyn was known to have sporting hunts of those descended from the dragons.

title: Darksign
snippet:
Centuries after this abuse, the First Flame started to naturally fade out, and the Darksign, which used the power of the Flame to contain the Dark Soul, weakened too, leading humans to come back to life as Undead, but also cursing them to eventually become Hollows, as the Darksign would consume their Humanity still forced on their bodies.
Thus, Gwyn sacrificed himself to rekindle the First Flame and forcibly postpone the end of the Age of Fire. Now with a martyr figure to use as powerful propaganda, the Undead Prophecy was spread throughout Lordran to encourage all who bear the Darksign to come to Lordran and claim powerful souls, making them worthy of filling the Lordvessel and succeed Lord Gwyn, rekindling the dying flame and prolonging the Age of Fire. The Chosen Undead would find themselves nearly hollow for several centuries after the rekindling of the First Flame, bearing the cursed mark of the Darksign, the greatest sin against humanity.

title: Lords
snippet:
Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - the_fast_fading_flame_and_the_birth_of_chaos 
 the_fast_fading_flame_and_the_birth_of_chaos : Gwyn found one day that the First Flame was fading, and that once it had burnt out the Age of Dark would begin.

The Lords feared the Dark, and sought to prolong the Age of Fire. The Witch of Izalith attempted to create a new flame. However, this new Chaos Flame grew out of control and consumed the Witch of Izalith and many of her children, soon forming into a creation known as the Bed of Chaos, which consumed Izalith and mutated most of the Witch of Izalith's remaining children into abominable creatures, while also turning her only son into a volcanic monstrosity. From the Chaos Flame came the race of Demons, against which Gwyn waged war. The Silver Knights that fought in this war were scorched and became the Black Knights.

title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Anor Londo (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - location - lore 
 lore : In the Age of Fire, Anor Londo was the "City of Gods" where Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight once ruled. Gwynevere and Gwyndolin, the children of Gwyn, also lived here.

title: Ring of the Sun's Firstborn
snippet:
Ring of the Sun's Firstborn -  Dark Souls - ring - description 
 description : Lord Gwyn's firstborn, who inherited the sunlight, once wore this ancient ring. Boosts the strength of miracles.

Lord Gwyn's firstborn was a god of war, but his foolishness led to a loss of the annals, and rescinding of his deific status. Today, even his name is not known.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: According to Darkstalker Kaathe, the Chosen Undead, protagonist of *Dark Souls*, is destined to bring about the Age of Dark, as they are the descendant of the Furtive Pygmy, who possessed the Dark Soul and divided it among early humans in the form of Humanity. Should the Chosen Undead abandon the First Flame to die out after the defeat of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, they will "usher in the Age of Dark", and become the fabled "Dark Lord" of whom Kaathe speaks. It is important to note that Kaathe tells the Chosen Undead that the Age of Dark had apparently already begun shortly before Gwyn chose to link the Flame, though it was seemingly ended and replaced by the Age of Fire when the Flame was linked.

title: Courland
snippet: At a certain point the First Flame began to fade again and the first Fire Keeper of Lothric had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a "barren plane of endless darkness". For this reason, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition, was called to become a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Defying his frail appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Champion, something for which he himself expresses remorse and asks to be forgiven. Despite his role, Ludleth was then exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric, ensuring that the first Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes and that all future maidens like her were deprived of their sight, to prevent them from observing the future without the light of the First Flame. The original eyes were hidden in a version of the Firelink Shrine on the verge of sinking into darkness and where the First Flame was an

title: Sunlight Medal
snippet:
Sunlight Medal -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : This faintly warm medal, engraved with the symbol of the Sun, is the ultimate honor, awarded to those who summon the Warrior of Sunlight and complete a goal.

The symbol represents Lord Gwyn's firstborn, who lost his deity status and was expunged from the annals. But the old God of War still watches closely over his warriors.

title: Humans
snippet:
Humans -  Dark Souls III - character - last_days_of_fire 
 last_days_of_fire : Many millennia—or even more—have gone by, and the linking of the Fire has become a staple in the world. Finally, when the new "Lord of Cinder" Prince Lothric was destined to sacrifice himself to the Flame, he refused and opted to watch the Age of Dark settle. To save the Age of Gods, four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected as Undead, but three of them either sought the Age of Dark, or no longer cared either way. One last contingency plan existed, to awaken the Unkindled, those who had previously failed to prolong the Age of Fire with their sacrifices. Kaathe's will has been reinterpreted by the Sable Church of Londor, who aim for a different Age of Dark than what Kaathe sought; an age ruled by a Lord of Hollows.

title: Undead
snippet:
Undead -  Dark Souls - mechanic - causes 
 causes : The curse of undeath was created when Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and Ruler of the Age of Fire, began to feel threatened by the descendants of the Furtive Pygmy: humans were immortal beings, born from the Dark yet able to live in a world enlightened by the Fire, whose souls did not lose power despite being endlessly split and multiplied. According to the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, the gods were intimidated by this unexplored potential of the Dark Soul. They had briefly glimpsed at the smidgen of life emanated from the primordial human knights, and feared the eventual overthrow of Anor Londo and its Age of Fire. Therefore, a complex and ingenious apparatus was set in motion with the goal to mould humanity into a subservient, weak people that would not only serve the Age of Fire, but also refused to relinquish it to make way for the Age of Dark.

title: McLoyf
snippet:
McLoyf -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : McLoyf is one of the members of Gwyn's clan who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire. He was worshiped by the humans as the god of medicine and alcoholic drinks and his face was even minted on the copper coins used by men.

After Lord Gwyn linked the First Flame and his firstborn son was dethroned and exiled, McLoyf abandoned Anor Londo together with nearly all of the other deities and moved to an unknown location in the world of men. It's likely that he is still revered by the Way of White in Thorolund, as Petrus will be the one to gift the Chosen Undead with coins bearing his visage.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: Lothric, the younger prince, was the destined Lord of Cinder, who was tasked with sacrificing himself as fuel for the First Flame to uphold the Age of Fire. The prince, born a sickly, frail child, was nevertheless viewed as the "last hope of his line", the culmination of generations of Lothric rulers obsessed with producing worthy Champions for the Flame. For the anticipated journey of the young prince to the Kiln of the First Flame, a platinum sword was crafted and blessed with strong magic by the High Priestess, long before he was ready to fulfill his destiny.

title: Souls of Lords
snippet:
Souls of Lords -  Dark Souls - item - lore 
 lore : The Souls of Lords were discovered by the chosen few that "came from the dark". Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, Nito, the First of the Dead, The Witch of Izalith and the Furtive Pygmy.

Gwyn, Nito and The Witch of Izalith used the power procured from the Lord Souls to challenge the Everlasting Dragons for dominion of the world and, with the help of others, were successful in their endeavor.

The Witch of Izalith attempted to recreate her own First Flame by using her Lord Soul, but this resulted in her own demise and the creation of the Bed of Chaos, mother of all Demons, who inherited possession of the Soul.

Bequeathed Lord Soul Shards are fragments of Gwyn's Lord Soul and were bestowed as gifts. One was given to Seath the Scaleless for betraying his own kind. Another was given to the Four Kings when Lord Gwyn recognized their foresight as leaders of New Londo.

title: Chosen Undead
snippet: ***Dark Lord:** This ending is unlocked if the player leaves the arena after killing Lord Gwyn. Upon leaving, the Chosen Undead is greeted by the Primordial Serpents, who bow down before their Dark Lord. Rejecting the Age of Fire, the Chosen Undead instead ushers in the Age of Dark, and becomes a monarch of mankind.

title: Age of Ancients
snippet:
Age of Ancients -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : In the Age of Ancients the world was undistinguished and covered in fog: a land of gray rocks, great trees and everlasting dragons; everything was the same and time didn't exist.But at some point the First Flame appeared and brought "disparity" into the world, allowing the existence of everything and its opposite: heat and cold, life and death, light and dark.

It was during this time that the Lord Souls were found near the Flame. The three Lords who found them (Nito, Gwyn and the Witch of Izalith) formed a coalition and used the power of their newly discovered souls to challenge the Dragons, starting a very long and destructive war. However, there was a fourth Lord Soul, the Dark Soul, which was found by the Furtive Pygmy. The only known act via this Lord was the fragmentation of their soul becoming the birth of Humanity, who would fight side by side with the Lords.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
Knight Artorias -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Sir Artorias was among the premier knights at the service of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight. Thanks to his unmatched skill with a greatsword and his indomitable will, he went on to become part of Gwyn's most trusted warriors, being granted a special soul. Artorias, along with Ornstein, Ciaran and Gough, thus formed the Four Knights of Gwyn; as a symbol of his association with the order, he was bestowed a magical ring with the wolf symbol, which strengthened his poise, making his fighting style with a greatsword more effective.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: What exactly the term "Age of Dark" implies is never made explicitly clear in the games, however it is stated in the canonical *Dark Souls Trilogy Compendium* to be a time when the Light fades, a Dark Lord is heralded, and humanity dominates the world. When the protagonists are given information about the Age of Dark, it typically comes from the mouths of potentially unreliable narrators, of whom Kaathe and his counterpart, Kingseeker Frampt, are examples. Kaathe asserts that the Age of Dark is "the age of men," presumably meaning the Age of those possessing Humanity in contrast to the Age of the Gods, and also declares that Gwyn "resisted the course of nature" when he linked the Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In *Dark Souls III*, countless beings have prolonged the Age of Fire, preventing its end and holding off the coming of the Age of Dark. By the time the game begins, there are countless Lords of Cinder - those who successfully linked the First Flame before - and even more Unkindled who were unsuccessful. Eventually the one anointed to next link the Flame (and indeed, who was born for that very purpose), Prince Lothric, rejected the idea that the Age of Fire should be prolonged any further and instead desired to end what he called the "fire-linking curse." A contingency plan was then activated, in which previous Lords of Cinder were resurrected in hopes that they, who had linked the First Flame before, might do so again. However, by this time, the world that had been created during the Age of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. As a result of the prolonging of the current Age, the act of which seemingly constituted a rejection of the natural order, the material world

title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
Knight Artorias -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls_the_age_of_fire 
 dark_souls_the_age_of_fire : Dark Souls: The Age of Fire* is a comic book series published in 2018, depicting events explicitly stated to be non-canonical.
The prologue of *The Age of Fire* is set during the war waged against the Everlasting Dragons that ended the Age of Ancients and brought about the titular Age of Fire. During a devastating battle, a dragon burns alive most of a squad of Gwyn's Silver Knights, with only one, Arkon, lucky enough to have been missed by its attack. As Arkon stands frozen in terror, Artorias suddenly emerges and swiftly beheads the dragon before leaving without a word; Lord Gwyn coincidentally returns at this point, and, presuming that it is Arkon who has slain the dragon, congratulates and grants the title of "Dragonkiller" upon the Silver Knight, who is too shocked to correct him.

title: Ring of the Sun's First Born
snippet:
Ring of the Sun's First Born -  Dark Souls III - ring - description 
 description : Ring of the Sun's first born, who inherited the light of Gwyn, the first lord.

Greatly boosts miracles.

The Sun's first born was once a god of war, until he was stripped of his stature as punishment for his foolishness. No wonder his very name has slipped from the annals of history.

title: Dark Lord
snippet: The interpretation of the Dark Lord's role in founding a new world order seems to have varied over time. The "Dark Lord" ending of *Dark Souls I* entails abandoning the First Flame to die out and beginning a new age from naught; the "Usurpation of Fire" ending of *Dark Souls III* however is somewhat different. Many millennia past the time of the Chosen Undead, the Sable Church of Londor, founded by three sisters who were disciples of Kaathe, are searching for a worthy Lord of Men. If the Ashen One cooperates with Yuria, a sister of the Sable Church, they are asked to "usurp the Flame", to "wrest it from its mantle". In doing so, the Ashen One would inherit what little lifeforce remains of the First Flame, and thus become a worthy Lord of Men—that is, a "Lord of Hollows", as it has come to be referred to. By this time, the notion that Hollows were the "true face of man" had become more accepted, propagated especially by the Pilgrims of Londor, melding the two titles of Dark Lord into

title: The Duke's Archives
snippet:
The Duke's Archives -  Dark Souls - location - lore 
 lore : The library is home to Seath the Scaleless, and was granted to Seath by Gwyn, along with a Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard, as a reward for aiding in the birth of the Age of Fire.

It is here that Seath delves into his experiments and studies. The Six-Eyed Channelers found here are servants of Seath, seeking and kidnapping inhabitants of Lordran for his research. The Pisaca are among the results of these experiments.

Archive Tower was turned to a prison; once it had a casual role of storing books. Cell below, now inhabited by Pisacas, once held countless maidens. Currently it is empty, apart from few key persons. Prison guardians are serpent men.

title: Humans
snippet:
Humans -  Dark Souls III - character - age_of_ancients 
 age_of_ancients : The Humans were created by the Furtive Pygmy, a forgotten Lord from the dawn of Fire, who claimed a small spark known as the Dark Soul. With this soul, the Pygmy raised up the Human race, binding their nature with the Dark. When the other Lords prepared to battle the Dragons, they came to the Humans, and conscripted them into their ranks. To this end, Humans began to forge arms and armor in the Abyss, which drew upon the power of a dark flame. Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, and his children, the Gods, cast a seal of fire upon them due to their perilous nature. So it was that the Human army, who were dubbed the Ringed Knights, set out with the Lords and their armies to eradicate the Everlasting Dragons, but due to their disruptive potential, their roles went unrecorded in histories.

title: Lords
snippet:
One of Gwyn's four knights, Artorias, and his wolf companion Sif made a covenant with the beings of the Abyss that allowed him to traverse it, so that he could hunt the Darkwraiths. Artorias later arrived in Oolacile in an attempt to combat the spread of the Abyss, but was overcome and was forced to sacrifice his greatshield to save Sif. This left him unprotected from the Abyss, and he later became corrupted and driven to madness.

The Way of White was usurped by Gwyn's uncle, Lloyd, who also would start hunts against the Undead.

Eventually, the undead were corralled into several asylums to await the end of the world, for it is prophesied by Astora - who themselves inherited the prophecy from Frampt - that one day an undead will escape the prison and succeed Gwyn in linking the fire. At the same time, Kaathe preaches that this chosen has the opportunity to become the new Dark Lord and usher in the Age of Dark.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Through their successful alliance against the Everlasting Dragons, Seath became a close friend to the Lord of Sunlight and was amply rewarded for his indispensable contributions to the war. He was wed into Gwyn's family as his son-in-law, inducting him into the nobility of the Gods, and was bestowed the honorific of "Duke". Gwyn further gifted Seath a fragment of his powerful Lord Soul and the Royal Archives, an enormous library towering above Anor Londo, which contained all the knowledge available to the city of the gods, leaving the dragon the freedom to do his own research; in time, the archives became so synonymous with Seath that they became known as "The Duke's Archives" instead.

title: Lothric
snippet: In the beginning, the first Fire Keeper had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a barren plane of endless darkness. Acting to ward off an Age of Dark, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition of Courland, rose to the challenge of becoming a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Despite his feeble appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Lord, something for which he himself expresses remorse, asking to be forgiven. Ludleth was exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric to ensure that the Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes, as well as all future maidens, to prevent them from observing a future without the Flame. The original eyes were sealed away in an enigmatic instance of Firelink Shrine, where the First Flame had all but gone out.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: Lothric, the younger prince, was the destined Lord of Cinder, who would sacrifice himself as fuel for the First Flame to uphold the Age of Fire. The prince, born a sickly, frail child, was nevertheless viewed as the "last hope of his line", the culmination of generations of Lothric rulers obsessed with producing worthy Champions for the Flame. For the anticipated journey of the young prince to the Kiln of the First Flame, a platinum sword was crafted and blessed with strong magic by the High Priestess, long before he was ready to fulfill his destiny. Oceiros created extensive propaganda around Lothric, not only giving him the name of the kingdom, but also building statues that depicted him with his sacred sword ready to complete his task, as well as preparing his throne at the Firelink Shrine in advance.

title: Ending
snippet:
Ending -  Dark Souls - mechanic - the_dark_lord 
 the_dark_lord : This ending is obtained after exiting the arena where the Chosen Undead felled Gwyn instead of lighting the bonfire. All the primordial serpents bow before the new ruler, the Chosen Undead, who has thus become the "Dark Lord". By choosing this ending, the Age of Fire is relinquished and Darkstalker Kaathe's goal of starting the Age of Dark is fulfilled.

title: Soul of Artorias
snippet:
Soul of Artorias -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Soul of Lord Gwyn's Knight Artorias, who was consumed by the Abyss.

The Legend that Artorias repelled the Abyss only told half of the story. It seems that he was defeated, and his honor preserved, by some unsung hero, who is the true victor over the Abyss.

title: Lost Izalith
snippet:
Lost Izalith -  Dark Souls - location - lore 
 lore : Izalith was once the domain of the Witch of Izalith, and was seemingly a great and booming city. However, when The Witch attempted to recreate the First Flame from her own Lord Soul, she failed to control it and was transformed into the Bed of Chaos. Izalith was subsequently overrun by the demons born from the Bed of Chaos. The demons fought against Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and his knights, were defeated, and after hearing Quelaag's cut dialogue, were apparently punished by being contained to their fallen city.

title: Old Ones
snippet:
Old Ones -  Dark Souls II - boss - old_iron_king_gwyn 
 old_iron_king_gwyn : The Old Iron King, wielder of the Old King Soul, after being killed by the Smelter Demon, was said to have succumbed to the flames and had his flesh charred, which became molten earth. This is a reference to how Gwyn, Lord of Cinder hurled himself into the First Flame to link the fire and prolong the Age of Fire, additionally, Sweet Shalquoir says that one of the Old Ones was "A vainglorious liar who ended up hurling himself into the flames" which makes a perfect pararel to Gwyn's linking of the fire, althrough it's unknown if she refers to the Old Iron King or the Soul Possessing him.

According to his Soul, when the Old Iron King succumbed to the flames, he was possessed “by a evil that lurked below”. This is likely how he acquired his Great Soul and the reason for his transformation into his current state.

Second playthroughs and onward cause the Old Iron King to drop the Old King Soul upon defeat.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: At some point, the Four Lords who had found immense Lord Souls and built their civilizations underground emerged to the surface with the intention of waging war against the Dragons and conquering the world for themselves. Seath decided to betray his race to ally with Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, and help the Lords in the war. He was instrumental in the gods' eventual victory, and the triumphant Lords would exterminate much of the Ancient Dragons, cementing their rule. Seath would also pillage the Ancient Dragons' sacred treasure, the Primordial Crystal, the centerpiece of his efforts to achieve immortality.

title: Lothric
snippet:
Lothric -  Dark Souls III - location - firelinking_duty 
 firelinking_duty : The tradition of linking the Flame plays a central role in Lothric, testified by the Firelink Shrine's location just outside the city walls, connected to the Royal Gardens. A large number of people throughout the long history of the kingdom came here to take part in the ritual initiated by Lord Gwyn's sacrifice. Those who failed, becoming the Unkindled, were buried near the Shrine in the Cemetery of Ash. Next to the Cemetery was an arena complete with stands, where Iudex Gundyr's golem judged those who aspired to become Lords, testing their strength. The ritual of the linking of the Flame permeated the kingdom at every level up to the royal family, who were obsessed with producing a worthy Champion in their line to preserve their divine mandate as the guardians of the Age of Fire.

title: Filianore
snippet:
Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Filianore is the last daughter of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight. Her sacred symbol is a crest of young grass.

She did not reside in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire unlike the other deities. Her father Gwyn, after winning the war against the dragons, "gave" Filianore as a gift to the Pygmy Lords together with a magnificent ringed city at the edge of the world. Before leaving her in the Ringed City, Gwyn promised her that he would come back for her some day.

Throughout the millennia that followed in the Age of Fire, the Pygmies worshipped Filianore as a goddess, building a church in her name with her as the matriarch. Even the Pygmy Lords who possessed the Dark Soul and ruled the city relied on her for salvation.

title: Furtive Pygmy
snippet:
Furtive Pygmy -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : The Furtive Pygmy is one of the primordial humanoids that appeared underground following the advent of the First Flame which brought "disparity"—heat and cold, life and death, light and dark. He was the one who found the Dark Soul among the four Lord Souls, the other three of which were discovered by Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, Gravelord Nito, and the Witch of Izalith.

The Furtive Pygmy fragmented his Dark Soul among his descendants, creating the first Humans in the form of the Pygmies. The pygmies harnessed their peculiar Lord Soul and unlocked the life-generating capabilities of its Abyss, forging weapons and armor that adopted the properties of darkness.

title: Gravelord Nito
snippet:
Gravelord Nito -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Nito is one of the primordial humanoid creatures that appeared underground after the First Flame appeared, which brought "disparity": heat and cold, life and death, light and dark. He was one of those who found the four Lord Souls, sources of immense power, together with Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, the Witch of Izalith and the Furtive Pygmy.

At some point Nito would die, but, thanks to the power of his soul, was able to come back to life with necromancy, becoming a living mass of conjoined skeletons, earning the title "first of the dead" ("dead" meant as a new species of skeletal creatures, not the first deceased being). Nito learned to harness the power of his Lord Soul to produce a dark power capable of bringing death to every living being, and he infused it in his Gravelord Sword, crafted from the bones of the fallen and exuding his miasma of death as a toxin lethal for any living being.

title: Grave Warden Agdayne
snippet:
Grave Warden Agdayne -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : As a Fenito, Agdayne watches over the Undead Crypt and its deceased to make sure they are properly kept in their rest and not disturbed. He was entrusted this task by "the one who gave us the first death". He mentions a "king of light" from an age long ago who was afraid that humans would bring forth an Age of Dark. The king he mentions is likely Gwyn, Lord of Cinder.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Four Kings -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : The Four Kings were once the great leaders of a country of humans. During the Age of Fire, Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight recognized their abilities and foresight and rewarded them with a fragment of his powerful Lord Soul and the title of kings, using his power to bind and hold close to him the powerful humans. The god also allowed them to build their civilization of New Londo near Anor Londo as a lower vassal of the city of the gods. Over time their city of humans grew to host countless lives, becoming a robust and flourishing culture. Although at some point the First Flame began to fade out, leading to the emergence of the Curse of Undeath, the city continued to exist and function as an Undead city, implying the good governance of the four kings who managed to adapt to the change.

title: The Deep
snippet:
It is unclear what would have become of Aldrich at the end of the Age of Fire. While the champion of the Deep has already been defeated when the Ashen One visits the Ringed City or the Dreg Heap, it seems that his visions of an incoming Age of Deep Sea were close to coming to pass, with the remnants of the world of Man bustling with the sunken, stagnated dregs of humanity, the malformed legacy of the Dark Soul which had been suppressed by the Darksign for millennia.

To prevent the advent of the Age of Deep following the weakening of the First Flame, the plan of the Sable Church of Londor has become to tear the Flame off its Kiln and preserve it within a Lord of Hollows who can exploit its power, freezing the state of the world thanks to their Dark Sigil.

title: Lothric
snippet: Lothric, the younger prince, was the destined Lord of Cinder, who would sacrifice himself as fuel for the First Flame to uphold the Age of Fire. The prince, born a sickly, frail child, was nevertheless viewed as the "last hope of his line", the culmination of generations of Lothric rulers obsessed with producing worthy Champions for the Flame. For the anticipated journey of the young prince, a platinum sword was crafted and blessed with strong magic by the High Priestess, long before he would fulfill his destiny. Oceiros created extensive propaganda around Lothric, not only giving him the name of the kingdom, but also building statues that depicted him with his sacred sword ready to complete his task, as well as preparing his throne at the Firelink Shrine in advance. However, the hopes of the royal family would soon fade, as Lothric remained a shriveled child from birth into adulthood, never even growing out of his baby clothes.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

Once Aldrich defeated Sulyvahn and took control of the city, McDonnell remained to watch over the old Cathedral where the saint was busy digesting Gwyndolin, establishing the covenant of Aldrich Faithful, passing on his dark sorceries to followers who brought him evidence of success in their task.

title: Gods
snippet:
Many Silver Knights since the Age of Ancients served Lord Gwyn and the other Old Gods of Anor Londo, well into the events of *Dark Souls III*. Their origins and species are never clearly explained.
Crossbreed Priscilla, hated by the Gods, was exiled to the Painted World of Ariamis hidden in Anor Londo. She was likely the hybrid daughter of Seath, and the mother of both Gwyndolin, with Gwyn as the father, and of Yorshka, from another father.
Pontiff Sulyvahn, a cleric born in another Painted World and who later came to Anor Londo, where he would forcefully take control of Irithyll from Gwyndolin, becoming its tyrannical ruler.

 age_of_ancients : In the Age of Ancients, the world was shrouded by fog, filled with grey crags and arch-trees, and ruled by the immortal Everlasting Dragons. The dragons were unmatched, but eventually, subterranean humanoids would discover a great power within the First Flame, giving them the means to challenge the dragons.

title: Darkstalker Kaathe
snippet:
Darkstalker Kaathe -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Darkstalker Kaathe greets the Chosen Undead and tells his side of the story: that the player is not to renew the Age of Fire by rekindling the First Flame, but is in fact the descendant of the one who possessed the "Dark Soul", and shall be responsible for bringing about the Age of Dark. Kaathe will transport the player to Firelink Altar in order to place the Lordvessel, and then instructs the player to collect the other Lord Souls in order to confront Gwyn, Lord of Cinder.

Kaathe can initiate players into the Darkwraith covenant.

title: Liliane
snippet: Liliane is a founding mentor of the Sable Church, and the youngest sister to Elfriede and Yuria. The three sisters at one point entered into the service of the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, becoming his maidens. The Primordial Serpent taught them his art of the Dark Hand, which could sap the essence of its victims. The sisters pursued Kaathe's goal of ending the Age of Fire founded by the gods and ushering the Age of Dark, and searched for a Dark Lord whom they would empower to usurp the First Flame and use its powers to lead humans into a new age. To this end, the three sisters used their battle prowess to establish the Sable Church, an organization that claimed to offer salvation to Hollows. The Church became a haven for those with unsavory or blurry pasts, along with other rejects of the Age of Fire. An increasing number of Undead and Hollows flocked to the Church, forming a society of wretchedly aged, deceitful, deeply detested Hollows. Their realm would be known as Londor, where

snippet:

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
None of them will slow down when in the water at the bottom of the arena, unlike the player character.
Even at lower levels of NG+, this boss fight becomes one of the most challenging ones in the game, as the three enemies can all kill the player in only a few hits. In addition to that, the player cannot attack the same enemy for more than a few hits without them rolling away, especially when they have no means of stunlocking them or dealing consistent damage through ripostes or backstabs, making this fight incredibly tough. All of this makes summoning other players or NPC phantoms a very good idea.
