title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Toxic and poison work well on all three of them, allowing high damage to be dealt at relatively low risk.

When pursuing the player in melee, the bosses are willing to chase them over the arena's ledges into the water. They tend to hesitate at the edge before jumping, and when landing will pause for a moment even after they're no longer locked into the landing animation. Thus, goading the bosses into chasing you over these edges is a reliable way to get a safe, if small opening to hit them after they land, to get a slight lead over Varg and the Graverobber in their pursuit of you with which to get a hit in on Cerah, or to hit them with ranged attacks when they linger at the top of the ledge. Be careful not to stand directly below any of the bosses when doing this, as they can perform plunging attacks on you.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet: The AI pathing also seems to have a slight preference for taking the ramps down instead of jumping off the ledges, so if you jump off while the bosses aren't particularly close or, after dropping, wander too far from the edge closest to the bosses or too close to the ramp, they may opt to take the ramp instead. This pathing preference is not terribly strong, you do not need to wait until the last second to jump off or hug the wall after jumping, just don't drop when your pursuers are halfway across the room or start running for the ramp before they've followed you over the edge.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategies 
 strategies : Cerah the Old Explorer will shoot the player constantly if left alive while dealing with the other two, so it is helpful to either take him out first or move toward him in order to make him draw his Estoc. If left alone to shoot at the player, Cerah has incredibly high damage potential, as he is likely to stagger the player on top of doing high damage, indirectly increasing the damage output of both Varg or the Graverobber. Cerah is the most agile of the three, being able to consistently dodge many attacks, including backstabs. Attacking Cerah will cause his other two team members to charge at the attacker.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet: Another good strategy is to use the NPC summons Ruined Aflis and Rapacious Andrei to distract either Graverobber or Varg, preferably both, then repeatedly backstab them while they focus on the summons. They will likely turn their attention back to you afterward, but retreating or switching targets can cause them to focus on the summons again, allowing the strategy to be repeated. It is still important to watch for Cerah’s arrows while doing this. Once Graverobber and Varg are defeated, Cerah will be left alone, making the end of the fight much easier, especially if one or both summons are still alive. Or if preferred, focusing on Cerah after just one of his allies is killed in an attempt to eliminate the arrows. Again, the summons should keep the other distracted if you choose to do it this way.

 lead : The , , and are a trio of bosses in *Dark Souls II: Crown of the Sunken King*.

Found at the end of the Cave of the Dead, a location past the Priestess' Chamber bonfire in [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Shulva,_Sanctum_City Shulva], they are all fought at once and each have their own individual health bar.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Ancient Solder Varg uses equipment associated with Havel the Rock: Havel's Set, the Dragon Tooth, and Havel's Greatshield.

Cerah the Old Explorer dons a mixture of sets, namely the Lucatiel's Mask headwear part of Lucatiel's Set, the Black Leather chest armor part of the Black Leather Set, and the Leather Gloves and Leather Boots part of the Hunter's Set. His main weapon is a Dragonslayer Greatbow, although he will switch to an Estoc thrusting sword if the player gets close; he only ever wields one of these two weapons, using both hands.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
All three are capable of backstabbing the player. This means caution should be taken while healing. They move slower than the player while in the water, which can be used as an advantage to get away from them, although this can become a disadvantage if Cerah's line-of-sight is not broken.

They are very susceptible to being "pancaked" by 2-handed great hammers, the only exception being Varg while he's attacking. With good positioning, you can even pancake Varg and the Graverobber together, and keep squashing them as they get up, as long as Cerah doesn't have line of sight to shoot you. This is probably the fastest way to end the fight.

Toxic and poison work well on all three of them, allowing high damage to be dealt at relatively low risk.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
The Afflicted Graverobber is a very powerful enemy, causing heavy bleed buildup and being able to catch the player in a stunlock. The damage potential she possesses is phenomenal. The Graverobber will work alongside Varg in a melee situation, stunning the player, then having Varg follow it up with a smash. This is best avoided by trying to separate them and taking them on one at a time.

Ancient Soldier Varg is by far the hardest to topple of the three enemies. Should he reach lower than half of his health, he will begin healing with an Estus Flask. He spends most of his time blocking with his greatshield, though, meaning there will be multiple opportunities to guard break him. He will attempt to work as a tank for his comrades, constantly trying to get in the way to take as much damage for them as he can.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet:
Corvian (Lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : In the time of Lothric, more Corvians are seen outside the painting, some of them even acting as storytellers who share tales of their frigid home. Their stories are considered heretical, and most of their listeners are Corvians themselves. All of them have no place to go, and seemingly yearn to return to the frozen landscape of their painting.

These aren't the only descendants of the Crow People, however, and many of them still exist within a new Painted World, restored by Father Ariandel. He appears to be a large humanoid akin to a Giant, but shows some crow-like features across his body, like fuzzy legs and talon-like hands. It's unclear if he was one of the Corvians, but he was one of the more important figures of their society. The most important one by far was the mistress of the Painted World, who wielded a great scythe, which became a symbol of a long-lost home to the forlorn corvids.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet:
Corvian (Lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : By the time of Drangleic, knowledge of the Painted World had been lost. Regardless, some of its Corvian inhabitants took their leave, as one of their descendants, Weaponsmith Ornifex, can be found in the old town of Tseldora. Her choice to live in Tseldora seems rather curious, as the town has some passing connection to the ancient Goddess of Sin. It's unclear if she even knows of her and how relevant she used to be to her people.

She uses a special forging technique that originated from a strange being that once inhabited the area, though she is unaware of what it truly was. She also believes humans to be inherently different than her kind, suggesting that across the ages, the Crow People had forgotten that they originated from humans. This was probably not helped by the general distrust humanity displays when dealing with creatures who are different than them.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet: Now, many of the Corvian Settlers are being slaughtered by their knights for disagreeing with Friede's decision, and the people's opinion of her had turned sour. The Corvians suffered under the effects of the rot, many shriveling up, unable to move their legs, or festering with poison. Most of them drag tails made of feces, strung together by undigested plant matter. Only the coming of a second Ash can set things right, and that is what the forlorn Corvians and other inhabitants of the Painted World desire more than anything.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet:
Corvian (Lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : Corvians are transformed humans, warped by their obsessive devotion to Velka, Goddess of Sin. They are surprisingly varied in appearance, varying in how humanoid or bird-like they are. The earliest ones had lanky, androgynous bodies with crow heads, large wings replacing their arms, and red feet, while the later ones looked like emaciated humanoids with feathered legs and bird-like feet, capable of sprouting wings separate from their arms, though they lacked any real corvid feature in their faces. Lastly, most of the ones living in the painting, deprived of wings and sporting a few scattered feathers, but with an undeniable bird head with desaturated white eyes. Their knights are like a mix of this latter type and the very first one, showing a lanky yet imposing frame, while having no wings of their own. They are characterized as being unwanted, forlorn beings with no place to call home.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet: She is also the only Corvian that can be met in Drangleic, found in the clutches of the Lion Clan, who live in the nearby Shaded Woods. It's very likely more Corvians were travelling the world, but they are never met by the Bearer of the Curse.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet: However, Corvian society would split when the painting began rotting, just as it had long ago. Most of the settlers wished for the painting to burn like the time before, so that a new one could be restored in its place. Friede, however, couldn't let go of the world that had become her home, convincing Ariandel to bury the flame and enlisting the Corvian Knights to protect the painting from fire. She even had her enforcer, Sir Vilhelm, hide away the Painter who was meant to see flame, just to ensure the world wouldn't be burnt to cinders.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet:
Corvian (Lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : The Corvians have humble beginnings. Once, they were simple human worshippers of the Goddess Velka, who transformed through their devotion. In the time of Lordran, they were best known as Crow People of Velka, or simply Crow Demons. Despite being called "demons", they share no relation with the Chaos Demons of Izalith, as they were ultimately human in nature.

At some point, these devotees would find themselves in the Painted World of Ariamis, either banished there or simply seeking an escape from the real world, along with many of Velka's artifacts and a peculiar crossbreed child. Whether they transformed before setting foot within the painting or afterwards is unclear, but their presence was entirely localized within the frigid landscape, with none of them found elsewhere in this age. They are hostile to all those who enter the painting and don't belong there.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet:
Despite retaining their crow-like appearance, no mention of Velka is made, and her artifacts are nowhere to be found. This possibly hints at the fact that her original followers have lived and evolved for so long that they've completely forgotten about their past. It seems to be exactly the case, as the inhabitants of the painting even regard the people outside as foolish and inherently different than them.

The mistress of the Painted World vanished long ago, leaving the Corvians in search of someone to fill that void. They would find it in Elfriede, a woman from Londor and ex-member of the Sable Church, whom abandoned it all after becoming Ash. She found a home within the painting and vowed to protect its inhabitants by taking a similar role to the previous mistress. This endeared her to many of the Corvians, some of whom even swore themselves as knights to her. Ariandel, too, was charmed by her devotion to the forlorn.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - notes 
 notes : Gwyndolin's corridor is not infinite and has a certain length. If he is forced to the end of the corridor, he won't be able to teleport anymore and will be at the player's mercy. He will attack relentlessly, trying to defend himself, but as his attacks are mostly designed for long range battle, just circling him will make most of them miss.
Defeating Gwyndolin grants Domhnall the ability to sell the Moonlight Set; most notably his helmet, which increases the power of all magic.
The Darkmoon Knightess will become hostile if Gwyndolin has been challenged, regardless of whether he was defeated or not.

snippet:
Both the Orb and Arrow Spread attacks are avoidable by hiding behind one of the pillars on either side of the corridor. The Sphere Shot, on the other hand, will go through walls, inflicting full damage if not blocked or avoided. The Orb Spread and Sphere Shot are Magic-based, though, so a shield that can block 100% physical damage and has good Magic resistance, like the Crest Shield, is recommended for this fight.

If a player does not want to risk it too much, a good strategy to catch up to him is by moving from pillar to pillar until they are about two pillars away from Gwyndolin and then wait until he shoots his Arrow Spread. A Demon Prince, a champion of their race, challenged Prince Lorian of Lothric, only to be defeated and retreat without his memory of the flames. No longer able to pursue the rekindling of the Chaos Flame, the demon race was condemned to extinction; as time went on, even the few remaining demons all but lacked any trace of the flame within; one such lost demon, reduced to little more than a wood and stone golem, served as a gatekeeper of Lothric.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: By the time of the awakening of the Ashen One, the Flame of Chaos had begun to fail, making the ancient Demons a dying race. The ruins of Izalith are littered with huge piles of corpses of ancient Demons, most of them belonging to lesser Capra Demons and Taurus Demons, while few surviving specimens aimlessly roam a world that has no place for them. These beings, called Stray Demons, look like their ancestors only superficially since their body is smaller and made mostly by rock, wood and lava (much like the Bed of Chaos). They have decayed and petrified to the point of being able to spew mere boulders, instead of flames. The Batwing Demons, a lesser breed of ancient Demons, were unfazed by the Chaos Flame's extinction and kept their duty as "ferrymen" for those who followed the legacy of Gwyn (thus proving a deep connection between their kin and the Gods).

Beings twisted by Chaos into something else, like the Bed of Chaos or the Burnt Ivory King (as the Flame of Chaos would survive past the Bed of Chaos' death) are not categorized as Chaos Demons, as the term applies only to beings conceived by the Bed itself. The Bed's eventual demise in *Dark Souls* means that Demons, who cannot reproduce, now exist in a finite number, and by the time of *Dark Souls III* they are a dying race, close to extinction. Besides Chaos Demons are cretures also called 'demons' despite being fundamentally different in their origins, likely due to individuals being unaware of the distinctions.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: As a symbol of their dedication they became Egg Burdened, welcoming the parasitic eggs produced by Quelaag's sister into their bodies. In this way the eggs would hatch inside them, first producing Vile Maggots which would then develop into Giant Mosquitoes and ultimately into smaller insectoid demons: the Cragspiders. Quelaag's plan, with the help of her sister, was therefore to reproduce in miniature a version of the Bed of Chaos that would use humanity as fertilizer for eggs and the undead as hosts to create new, albeit lesser, demons. To receive help in their goal they even created the covenant of the Chaos Servants, which would welcome servants of the Daughter of Chaos with the aim of accumulating humanity by killing other Undead which they would then give to Quelaag's sister and in exchange get the chance to learn their pyromancies and a shortcut to their hometown of Lost Izalith.

Demon (lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : **Demons** are a race in the *Dark Souls* universe.

"True" Demons (labelled **Chaos Demons** in this article), are beings (some unique, others members of specific sub-species) originating from the fall of Izalith prior to *Dark Souls*, during which the Witch of Izalith lost control of her Lord Soul, causing the creation of the Flame of Chaos that twisted beings in Izalith and turned the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, a creative force that kept on endlessly making new lifeforms: Demons, which spilled from Izalith into the world. They typically have affinities for fire and/or stone.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet:
In the region of Drangleic several creatures are addressed as "demons" despite the fact that they are not part of the life generated by the Bed of Chaos:
** The Covetous Demon was once a man whose deep affection for Queen Mytha was unrequited. Despite this he never left the queen and, entranced by some perverse love, he started to devour all thing and even humans in an expression of desire, gorging himself to the point of transforming into a monstrous creature.
**The Demon of Song was once a man that was unable to resist the temptations of the flesh and developed a taste for humans, to the point of transforming into a monstrous creature.
**The Smelter Demon was a mass of iron, one of the constructs given life by the Old Iron King when he obtained the power to grant life to heaps of iron and molded a great array of metallic automatons with a soul.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet:
Demon (lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : After The Witch of Izalith found an immense and powerful Lord Soul near the First Flame, she pooled her and her daughters' newfound strength into aiding fellow Lords in winning the war against the Dragons and built their civilization underground. They continued to experiment with the power of fire and souls; at a certain point, driven by ambition and arrogance, Izalith, using her own Lord Soul as a basis, tried to recreate the First Flame, the primordial force that had brought life into the world. This, however, was not entirely successful, resulting in the Flame of Chaos, an unstable power that the witch was unable to control. She was initially consumed by it and became a beast of chaos fire along with two of her daughters: the "Bed of Chaos". This creature, fueled by the power of the Flame of Chaos, became a seedbed for a new life form: Demons.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet:
However the flames of Chaos would not be sated, and over time the Ivory King was drained of his vigour; sensing the degradation of his power, he decided to plunge into Chaos' heart in an attempt to reduce its flames alone but was devoured by the chaos, becoming an empty husk controlled by it. After their King was consumed by Chaos, many of Eleum Loyce's faithful knights decided to follow him and put him out of his misery but their souls too were corrupted by the flames, leading them to lose all sense of purpose and being, leaving them driven only by the urge of expunging any who might disturb the flames even if they were former compatriots. With their armor charred and burnt black by fire and still burning in agony, they remained as empty shells controlled by the Chaos alongside their once-proud king.

As a last resort to stem the advance of the Chaos that couldn't be contained, the decision was made to "fling open" the ivory gates of the fortress of Eleum Loyce.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: At one point Izalith, aiming to gain greater sway over the Flame of Chaos, lost all control of the power again and never regained it: Chaos engulfed the Lord and her daughters before scorching their city with them. Izalith and her two daughters directly involved in the experiment were left permanently scarred, reduced to a monstrous lignified creature anchored in the throne room at the center of the city. Of the daughters of Izalith, few managed to escape. Quelaag and her sister's lower bodies were molded into deformed demonic spiders and the flames of chaos engulfed them but they managed to escape the city and survive on its borders, carving out a domain for themselves. The only other survivor, who managed to avoid the corruption of chaos and retain a normal body, was Quelana, who remained in self-imposed exile around the ruins of her country for centuries.

title: Explorer

For restocking the items, Merchant Hag Melentia carries more Lifegems and Witching Urns and 1 more Pharros' Lockstone, Laddersmith Gilligan has Aromatic Oozes, Wood Bolts are sold by Blacksmith Lenigrast, Repair Powders are sold in limited quantities by Blacksmiths and infinitely by one late-game merchant, Prism Stones are sold by Sweet Shalquoir, and 5 more Rusted Coins are sold by Magerold of Lanafir.

Their high Adaptability gives them 9 i-frames when starting out, and they only need 2 more points in the stat to improve that to 10 i-frames.

title: Explorer
snippet:
The Traveling Merchant Set is only a bit better than the Imported Set and has no Poise but the hat increases Item Discovery slightly, which is a solid benefit early on.

The lone Pharros' Lockstone can be used to unlock 1 (and only one, since it is a consumable) Pharros' Contraption. Of the first two Contraptions to be found in the game, the first one is below a trapped room with ballistae in the Forest of Fallen Giants and used to get the Chloranthy Ring and a Titanite Slab, and the second one is found one a small platform up halfway up the first set of stairs in No-man's Wharf where it is used turn on the lights and scare away all the Dark Stalkers in the area.

title: Explorer
snippet:
Explorer -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Explorer** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It has no particular specialty, with only high Adaptability and an above average Vitality being notable. It is, essentially, a Deprived with some extra stats, some bonus items, and a Dagger.

As their Dagger is the only weapon they start out with, with not even a spell to help them, it is imperative to pick up a second Dagger in Things Betwixt on the first side path fore more Durability. Is is possible to wield the Morning Star from the cliffs in Majula two-handed with 2 more points in Strength and one more point in Dexterity, and a Light Crossbow can be found atop a wall in the Forest of Fallen Giants and only need 1 more point in Strength to wield with two hands.

The Traveling Merchant Set is only a bit better than the Imported Set and has no Poise but the hat increases Item Discovery slightly, which is a solid benefit early on.

title: Explorer
